transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. A lazy yellow flame that leaves soot means the back burner isn't burning its gas cleanly, because the gas and air aren't mixing properly at the burner. Based on what you've described, the most likely reason is the burner cap or its ports, either not sitting square or being dirty, wet or blocked. From what you have described, the most likely cause is burner cap and ports seating / cleanliness. The usual cause is a burner cap that isn't sitting square, or one that's wet or greasy after cleaning. Lift off the cap and crown, dry and clean them (and gently wipe the white igniter tip), then re-seat them so they sit flat. Was a cap out of place, wet or dirty (and is it sorted), or were they all seated, dry and clean?
[Safety panel] If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.

The cap looks to be seated properly and isn't wet, but there are some burnt spills around it. I should also say that I've noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.
